result.title: QUBO-based feature selection for MRI undersampling pattern design
result.summary: We formulate undersampling mask design for Cartesian magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) as a feature subset selection problem. Each sampling line is represented by a binary feature indicating whether it is included in each candidate mask. Using candidate masks and their training-set evaluations, we estimate mutual information (MI) and conditional mutual information (CMI). These estimates and a sampling-count penalty define a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) model. The model is solved using simulated annealing and quantum annealing to determine a feature subset and its corresponding sampling mask. We assess the selected subsets on the test set through zero-filled reconstruction in Fourier undersampling simulations using fastMRI knee magnitude reference images, with patient-disjoint training and test sets. At all six tested target sampling rates from 15% to 40%, the resulting reconstructions have lower mean root mean square error than those obtained with four conventional sampling methods. They also have higher mean structural similarity than those obtained using univariate mutual-information ranking at all tested rates. These results support information-theoretic feature selection as an approach to MRI undersampling mask design under the tested zero-filled simulation settings.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文把笛卡尔 MRI 欠采样掩膜设计表述为二值特征子集选择问题：用候选掩膜的互信息与条件互信息估计，加上采样数惩罚构造 QUBO 模型，以模拟退火和量子退火求解，并在 fastMRI 膝部数据上通过零填充重建与四种常规采样方法比较误差与结构相似度。
